The resolution curve is 7 [7, 7] for sonnet at every n (bounding anchors certify from 25 q; the mid anchors at 0.505 / 0.510 cannot certify at any n: 31,001 / 7,549 question-pairs) and 6 -> 4 -> 4 -> 3 for gpt-4o-mini, whose remaining (iii) tier is deepseek at key gap 0.0199 vs 0.017. PLACEMENT-CURVE as priced cannot narrow sonnet and is DECLINED; a further-step placement design is the registration to write.

one further bisection step per separable tier removes the separable tiers: placement cost is 400 + 100 per separable tier per newcomer; the residual is the structural floor (i) + (ii); criterion (22) is reachable for mid-board newcomers, not for a frontier newcomer.

plain_description.what: Places two new models (claude-3-5-sonnet, gpt-4o-mini) live into the existing 19-model leaderboard. Each is compared against 4 incumbents chosen by bisection, with 100 questions each: 400 matches per newcomer, 1,600 calls.
plain_description.why: Tests whether a new model can be ranked cheaply, within 2 adjacent tiers, without re-running the whole arena.
plain_description.information: A tight interval would make 400 matches a valid, cheap placement budget. Result: done, failed by the registered falsifier. Both placements point the right way and contain the true tier, but the intervals are too wide (7 and 3 tiers). A later re-analysis split the width into two parts. Part comes from frontier models the record refuses to order, a floor that no budget can remove for a frontier newcomer. Part comes from incumbents the newcomer was never judged against, which more bisection steps would remove. So 400 matches is not a placement budget. This belongs to the older question pool, which is now ruled history, not evidence.
